messages:
maria: Ran overnight shadow runs comparing FP8-KV-only vs INT8-KV-only on a prod-like 8h mixed prompt trace. Dropped raw logs to s3://redwood-shadow/kv/1725552468 and paste a short perf+quality summary below.
omar: Nice — any accuracy/regression signal to be worried about?
maria: Small deltas. FP8-KV shows +0.3% EM on long-context QA cases, but ~-0.6% on short-context paraphrase cases. Overall micro-avg change ~ -0.1% (within noise). Memory: FP8 saves ~12% on KV footprint.
ken: Latency numbers?
maria: Median token-latency: int8=3.2ms, fp8=2.9ms. p95: int8=14.8ms, fp8=16.2ms. So FP8 improves median but hurts tail. We also saw cold-start tail spikes for FP8 after cache invalidations.
jen: Hypothesis on tail source?
omar: My guess: dequant cost on reads + GC/eviction interactions. FP8 dequant path seems to have a heavier per-chunk CPU penalty at high concurrency.
maria: We observed a "dequant waterfall" in traces when KV occupancy > ~75% and eviction rates increase — dequant per-chunk jumps. Small snippet from traces and bench command: 

```bash
# reproduce
python bench_kv.py --model rwd-7b --kv-quant fp8 --trace traces/2026-03-19-mix.csv --concurrency 64
```

logs:
```
[03:12:11] worker-7 dequant-chunk ms=1.2
[03:12:11] worker-7 dequant-chunk ms=12.8  <-- spike coinciding with eviction
[03:12:11] worker-7 kv-evict idx=2345
```

luis: What is the absolute memory win for our common configs?
maria: For model ~30B equivalent: INT8-KV ≈ 14.0GB, FP8-KV ≈ 12.3GB (~1.7GB saved). For a 16-shard pool that's ~27GB total savings (not insignificant for infra ops).
ken: Given this tradeoff, what's the rollout plan?
maria: Proposal:
- Default to INT8-KV for high-concurrency prod pools (preserve tail SLOs)
- Offer FP8-KV as opt-in for dedicated low-concurrency or batched workloads
- Create an FP8 canary: route 1% traffic with `kv_quant=fp8` and auto-fallback to INT8 if p95 latency rises >10% or EM drops >1%
- Instrument dequant_kv_ms metric and alert on p95_dequant_ms > 10ms for 5m

jen: Also recommend synthetic warmup before roll (run prefix replay to populate KV) to avoid cold-evict spikes when enabling FP8.
sre-bot: alert created: `kv.dequant_tail` -> triggers when `p95(dequant_ms, 5m) > 10ms` ; pager policy: on-call eng-sre.
omar: I'll take the kernel perf action — profile the dequant kernel paths and try to implement a fused-dequant path or SIMD fastpath. Assigning to @omar and @ken.
ken: Ack, I'll pair with Omar on the fused path prototype. If we can shave the dequant hotspot we can flip default for dedicated pools.
maria: Thanks. Next actions: 
- @omar: perf profile + micro-optimizations (due EOD+2)
- @ken: prototype fused-dequant (due EOD+4)
- @jen: set up FP8 canary config and dashboards (SLOs + EM/QA) (due EOD+3)
- infra: add canary policy to routing layer (ops ticket created)

jen: I'll create the canary dashboard and short-run AB job; will include synthetic warmup step.
luis: Can we also get a run vs GPTQ/AWQ where we quantize only KV vs whole-weights? curious about interaction.
maria: Good idea — add to backlog. For now prioritize KV-only since that gives most immediate memory wins with lowest model-quality risk.
omar: one more note: bench workloads that are batch-heavy (latency-insensitive) look great with FP8; tail problems mostly show up at high concurrency and low-latency SLOs.
maria: Summary: FP8-KV = good median & memory, but tail/dequant spikes need kernel and eviction mitigations. Ship plan = INT8 default + FP8 canary + optimize dequant.
ken: :thumbsup:
jen: ack
maria: scheduling profiler run tomorrow 12:00 PST. ping me if you want access to traces.
